summary: `collect --source river|rss|day` prints headlines as JSON lines {id, title, publication, url, techmeme_permalink, published_at, date} from only /river, /feed.xml and dated /YYMMDD/h2000 pages; url is always the publisher's own link (never a techmeme.com link or /goto/, /r/ redirect), RSS titles lose their '(Publication)' suffix, and RSS uses a conditional GET whose 304 prints nothing and exits 0.
reason: A collector keeping its own copy of Techmeme must stay off /search/ and the redirect paths, which robots.txt disallows, and must not re-download an unchanged feed. Techmeme times are US Eastern; dated pages show no times, so their published_at is null rather than a guessed hour, and date comes from the item's own id because a snapshot can carry items from the day before.
validated_outcome: Live: a conditional GET of /feed.xml with a stored ETag returned 304, printed nothing and exited 0. Fixture tests cover river, RSS and dated-page parsing, publisher-only URLs, the 304 path via --state and --etag, and that /search/ is never requested.
